The endpoint returned HTTP 401 and a WWW-Authenticate Bearer challenge referencing https://mcp.lawve.ai/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp. That metadata names https://auth.lawve.ai/ as authorization server, scopes_supported ["marketplace:read"], and bearer_methods_supported ["header"]. The separately supplied origin-level metadata names https://studio.lawve.ai, scope ["read"]. Studio metadata advertises authorization_code and refresh_token grants, token endpoint auth method none, S256 PKCE, and registration_endpoint https://studio.lawve.ai/connectors/oauth/register. The endpoint-path metadata and Studio metadata disagree about the authorization server and scope. Metadata for auth.lawve.ai could not be fetched due to certificate verification failure; token lifetime and revocation were not found.

D_server_side_logic.additional_logic: 1. Tool listings describe search and manifest retrieval as read-only; no official tool annotations (readOnlyHint, destructiveHint, idempotentHint, openWorldHint) or server code were available. 2. No server-enforced confirmation mechanism was found; no write action appears in the two Anthropic-listed names. 3. OAuth scope is inconsistent across endpoint metadata: marketplace:read at the endpoint-path descriptor versus read at origin metadata. Product-role inheritance, admin switches, client allowlists, redirect approval, token lifetime, and revocation were not documented. 4. Public skills are described as available through the global endpoint; the vendor also describes organization-private libraries and choices for internal/external access. No URL parameters, mode headers, environment split, or region-specific endpoint was found. 5. Tools are described as searching public catalogue entries and retrieving public skill instructions; vendor also says organizations can configure private resources. Field masking and data-path boundaries were not specified. 6. No request ceiling or result cap was published. Terms prohibit bypassing request limits but state no amounts. 7. Tool schemas and validation behavior were unavailable. 8. The privacy policy lists platform usage data and authorizations granted to connected assistants; it does not specify MCP-call audit logs, their retention, or an opt-out. 9. No feedback, rating, report, survey, or upsell tool was found in the listed tool names or descriptions. 10. Retrieved skill content carries practitioner-authored instructions into the agent context. The vendor says resources are reviewed, while its terms say review/publication is not an endorsement or guarantee. No server instructions were available. 11. Vendor says new and updated public resources reach assistants as published; whether past agent behavior affects results is unknown. 12. The vendor describes public and organization resources through the same MCP; no sub-server routing details were found. 13. No raw API, SQL, script, or arbitrary execution tool was found in the listed names.

Retrieve one public skill’s complete instructions and manifest.
Return filter values and counts for marketplace categories, jurisdictions, and languages.

E_aggregated.token_method: The hosted endpoint is closed and no verbatim tool definitions or initialize instructions were available. The anonymous endpoint request returned HTTP 401.
E_aggregated.human_can_agent_cannot: A human can browse, publish, organize, and review resources through the Lawve platform; the listed MCP tools cover catalogue search and skill-manifest retrieval, not resource creation or editing. Public resources can also be browsed without the MCP account. The agent's access to organization-private resources is not sufficiently specified to determine its full scope.

F_documentation.implementation_hints_not_enforced: The vendor says the assistant searches by topic, jurisdiction, or practice area and opens the full resource instructions before applying them. These are descriptions of intended workflow; the authenticated tool descriptions and server enforcement could not be inspected.
F_documentation.governance_promises: The vendor says organization teams can share resources internally and choose selected material and read/contribute access for external users. Its privacy policy says personal data is hosted in the EEA and lists retention periods for platform data. Terms state that content review or publication is not an endorsement or guarantee.
F_documentation.promises_to_user: The vendor advertises free public catalogue access, updated resources as soon as published, and organization libraries built from the organization's data. It says internal shared libraries keep data inside the organization.
F_documentation.comparison_with_server_logic: The endpoint's OAuth challenge confirms authentication is required, and the metadata exposes a read-oriented scope, but no server code or authenticated behavior was available to verify the access-control, isolation, freshness, or data-location promises. Public descriptions and legal terms supply the remaining claims.

contradictions: Endpoint-path OAuth metadata names https://auth.lawve.ai/ and scope marketplace:read, while the origin-level protected-resource metadata names https://studio.lawve.ai and scope read. Studio's authorization-server metadata is available and advertises registration and PKCE; auth.lawve.ai metadata could not be fetched because of a TLS certificate error.

Anthropic's directory, Manufact, and Agentman report two Lawve tools, while the MCP App Store lists a third Lawve-named tool, lawvable_list_filters. The vendor publishes no tool-name list to resolve the difference.

The vendor page says the MCP can expose organization-private resources and external read or contribute access; the endpoint-path OAuth metadata advertises only marketplace:read. Whether that metadata describes only the public endpoint scope or is inconsistent with the organization feature is undocumented.
observations_for_research: The vendor's public description frames MCP as a gateway to practitioner-authored methods: search discovers resources and retrieval brings their instructions into the model context.
The product page describes a single MCP serving public resources and organization-managed libraries, with access choices for external sharing.
The endpoint is OAuth-protected even though the vendor describes the public catalogue as free and the resources as publicly available.
notes: Checked the supplied links.json, pages/ snapshots, links_check.txt, and code/GITHUB_COMMITS.txt; no official repository or package was listed. The endpoint's own page returned HTTP 401; /mcp/install returned 404. No official tool-reference page or tool-name list was found. Third-party catalogues used for tool names: Anthropic directory, Manufact, Agentman, and MCP App Store; the latter's ekstra tool is catalogue-only. MCP.so reported no live tool list. Unofficial server evidence was not used. Studio OAuth metadata conflicts with the endpoint-path resource metadata. The auth.lawve.ai metadata fetch failed certificate verification. Reviewed vendor MCP, connectors, privacy, and terms pages; no token lifetime, revocation, exact rate limits, or MCP-specific logging details were found.
